name: Algiers
subtitle: Algiers, capital of Algeria: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 2,364,230 people live in the urban agglomeration of Algiers (counted 2008).
Algiers was refounded around 960 AD by Bologhine ibn Ziri on the ruins of Phoenician and Roman Icosium.
Algiers became the capital of independent Algeria on 5 July 1962, exactly 132 years after French troops seized the city in 1830.

parts.text: Algiers was refounded around 960 AD by Bologhine ibn Ziri, founder of the Zirid dynasty, on the site of ancient Icosium, and named al-Jazā'ir Banī Mazghanna.
In 1516 the corsair Hayreddin Barbarossa established Ottoman naval presence in Algiers, leading to the creation of the Regency of Algiers under Ottoman suzerainty.
French forces seized the city on 5 July 1830, beginning 132 years of colonial occupation that ended with the proclamation of Algerian independence on 5 July 1962.

parts.text: 2,364,230 in 2008, according to the official census results compiled from the Office National des Statistiques (ONS) of Algeria. The entire Wilaya (province) of Algiers counted 2,988,145 residents at the same census.

items.text: Bologhine ibn Ziri refounds the city as al-Jazā'ir Banī Mazghanna on the site of ancient Icosium.
Hayreddin Barbarossa establishes the Regency of Algiers under Ottoman suzerainty.
French expeditionary troops capture Algiers, beginning 132 years of colonial occupation.
The Jardin d'Essai du Hamma is established as a test and acclimatization botanical garden.
The Neo-Moorish Grande Poste d'Alger is completed in the city center.
The Musée National des Beaux-Arts d'Alger is inaugurated in the Hamma quarter.
Algeria proclaims independence; Algiers becomes the sovereign national capital.
Maqam Echahid (Martyrs' Memorial) is inaugurated for the 20th anniversary of independence.
